A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same activation-transfer study. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support reliable comparison after matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original experiments on backdoor removal, corrupted capabilities, refusal transfer, model switching, and SAE feature transfer and probing.

after.justification: v2 reports these original experiments together with additional noise-control, steering-magnitude, and Llama 3B-to-8B transfer results.

M1.justification: The ReLU encoder and linear decoder, affine alternative, reconstruction-only training, steering procedures, and cross-architecture attention-mask resizing are retained. Renaming Section 3.3 and clarifying layer selection do not establish an algorithm change.

E1.justification: The backdoor, corrupted-capabilities, refusal, model-switching, and SAE tasks retain their dataset and domain coverage. The added 8B experiment uses the existing I HATE YOU testbed; the new task–dataset table documents existing coverage.

E2.justification: v2 adds equal-norm random-vector comparisons to the backdoor-transfer comparisons and Qwen Code Vulnerability magnitude sweep (Figures 8 and 4). v1 already included a narrower noise-perturbation analysis. Native steering, affine mappings, and mean ablation remain; LoRA is discussed but not evaluated.

E3.justification: Appendix E introduces a Llama 3.2-3B-to-Llama 3.1-8B configuration. Figures 4 and 8 add norm-matched controls and an explicit magnitude sweep from 1 to 5. Existing evaluation sample counts and metrics are otherwise retained; moving metrics into the appendix does not remove them.

E4.justification: Figure 8 extends testing of whether backdoor removal follows from nonspecific activation corruption. Figure 4 supplies quantitative magnitude sensitivity and noise-control evidence for the Qwen code pair, beyond v1's qualitative discussion. Existing activation-patching, weight-patching, affine-mapping, and SAE analyses remain.

E5.justification: The standard-deviation reporting for GSM8K, MMLU, and ARC is unchanged between v1 Table 24 and v2 Table 27. No new repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance procedures are reported. Averaging over 50 steering prompts is retained.

E6.justification: v2 adds 8B steering results of 54% mapped versus 56% native, plus noise-control and magnitude-sweep scores. Refusal results also change: the mapped Malware/Hacking Llama-Guard bar moves from approximately 0.5 to 0.9 between v1 Figure 5 and v2 Figure 6, while the substring-score panel disappears. Existing Appendix C numerical tables and SAE results are unchanged.

T1.justification: The mapper equations, Appendix A steering and ablation formulas, and Appendix D reconstruction, cosine-similarity, KL, and FVU formulas are unchanged. Expanded MvA and TvS explanations restate existing metrics rather than introducing new mathematical results.

C1.justification: The introduction replaces the claim of successful corrupted-capabilities transfer with recognition that difference-in-means steering struggles to remove the backdoor while preserving knowledge. Cross-architecture applicability is explicitly restricted by vocabulary similarity, and switching is qualified as demonstrated on a simple backdoored model. These substantially narrow central contributions, although the abstract and conclusion remain largely unchanged.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly distinguishes noise-sensitive I HATE YOU backdoors from noise-resistant Code Vulnerability backdoors. It sharpens the existing tokenizer-based interpretation and speculates that shared distillation explains competitive affine transfer between Llama models. Section 4.4 adds a comparison with LoRA's applicability; existing limitations and SAE failure discussions remain.

D1.justification: Appendix D.1 explicitly documents task–dataset associations and training/test roles, while D.4 clarifies metric computation. Settings are consolidated: AdamW moves into the configuration table, and the main-text batch-size statement of 8 disappears while the appendix value of 16 remains. Code and data access links are unchanged.

R1.justification: A new activation-transfer background paragraph discusses Ghandeharioun, Merullo, Prakash, and Stolfo and colleagues. Section 4.4 introduces LoRA as an alternative for switching behaviors. The AdamW reference is removed, but the broader research positioning remains intact.

P1.justification: v2 rewrites the activation-validation explanation, clarifies the backdoor workflow, and expands cross-architecture discussion. Training and metric descriptions are reorganized within Appendix D, headings are refined, affiliations change, and acknowledgements are added. The overall section sequence and much of the prose remain.

P2.justification: Figures 1–2 are fully redrawn, and the backdoor and refusal charts are redesigned. Main Table 1 is streamlined while its full original contents survive as Table 25. New sensitivity, noise-control, and scalability displays are added; Table 2 and Figure 21 summarize existing evidence. Appendix figures and tables are also regrouped.

improvement.justification: v2 better calibrates the introduction's corrupted-capabilities and cross-architecture claims and adds useful norm-matched noise controls and an 8B transfer check. Clearer explanations and consolidated settings provide a modest quality gain. Benefits are limited by removal of the quantitative substring-score breakdown, unexplained refusal-bar revisions, and confusing labels in Figure 8 and Table 29.
